hero.lead: A nation of 640,000 with forest across nine tenths of its land, where TotalEnergies took a $10.5 billion decision in October 2024 to develop the GranMorgu oil field, with first oil expected in 2028.

capital.heading: Oil to come, and a forest nation to plan for.

record.text: Final investment decision on the GranMorgu development, Block 58, 1 October 2024; first oil expected in 2028
Bank loan concluded by Staatsolie, the state oil company, on 14 May 2025 with 18 banks and financial institutions, to finance its 20% participation in GranMorgu
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Follow-on 8.50% dollar bond due 2035
register.detail: Ministry of Finance and Planning · a further issue of the 8.50% notes due 2035 · notes outstanding $1,315M in the notice of 7 April 2026, up from $1,050M in January 2026 (arithmetic: $265M)
register.note: The use of the proceeds is not stated in the Ministry’s notices
register.text: A further issue of the Republic’s 8.50% notes due 2035, which took the notes outstanding from $1.05 billion to $1.315 billion in early 2026. The Ministry’s notices give the amount but not the use of the proceeds, so the line is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards until a Ministry source states it.

register.name: Two dollar bonds due 2030 and 2035
register.detail: Ministry of Finance and Planning · closed 6 November 2025 · $525M of 7.70% notes due 2030 · $1,050M of 8.50% notes due 2035 · indenture of 6 November 2025
register.note: Funded the purchase of $419.8M of the 7.95% Cash/PIK notes due 2033 tendered in October 2025 and the redemption of the rest
register.text: Two bonds of the Republic of Suriname that refinanced its 7.95% Cash/PIK notes due 2033: the proceeds bought back and redeemed those notes, retire part of the Oil-Linked Securities and may prepay bilateral debt. A refinancing, it is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Staatsolie bank loan for its GranMorgu participation
register.detail: Staatsolie · concluded 14 May 2025 · 18 banks and financial institutions · finances a 20% participation in GranMorgu · repays an outstanding $130M bank loan
register.note: Staatsolie estimates that $2.4bn is required for its 20% participation
register.text: A loan from a consortium of international, regional and local banks to Staatsolie, the state oil company, to finance its twenty percent participation in the GranMorgu development and to repay an outstanding bank loan of $130 million. The participation gives a company owned by the state a direct share of the field, whose earnings could one day finance the seven standards.

register.name: Staatsolie bonds for its GranMorgu participation
register.detail: Staatsolie · issued March 2025 · for its 20% participation in GranMorgu
register.note: With the $1.6bn bank loan, own cash and cash flow, part of a $2.4bn requirement
register.text: Bonds issued by Staatsolie in 2025 to finance its twenty percent participation in the GranMorgu project, alongside the bank loan, its own cash and the cash flow of its business. With the loan, they give a company owned by the state a fifth of the field.

register.name: Trade finance facility with Finabank
register.detail: IFC Global Trade Finance Program · signed in Paramaribo 15 May 2026 · guarantees to international banks for trade transactions originated by Finabank · amount not disclosed
register.note: For local businesses, especially small and medium enterprises, that import inputs and export
register.text: IFC guarantees to international banks for letters of credit and other trade transactions that Finabank originates. The facility helps local businesses, especially small and medium enterprises, import the inputs they need, expand exports and create jobs, which carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility arrangement
register.detail: IMF · the Fund-supported programme concluded in March 2025 · 2025 Article IV consultation concluded by the Executive Board on 26 January 2026 · no current arrangement
register.note: IMF credit outstanding at 31 March 2026; engagement continues under the IMF’s Post-Financing Assessment framework
register.text: The IMF arrangement that supported Suriname’s stabilisation ended in March 2025, and no new arrangement is in place. In its 2025 Article IV consultation the IMF asks Suriname to raise the primary surplus while safeguarding priority investment in human capital, and to build the institutions to manage oil wealth once production begins.

register.name: Suriname Preparedness and Enhancing Resilient Communities Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 28 February 2025 · concessional loan · project P504548 · the first IDA financing for Suriname, a member since October 2024
register.note: Directly benefits 50,000 residents in and around Paramaribo and supports 35 communities, at least half of the initiatives women-led
register.text: A concessional IDA loan that upgrades drainage in Greater Paramaribo, home to 67 percent of the population, improves emergency preparedness and funds community-led resilience projects in Paramaribo, Saramacca and Wanica. Better drainage protects homes and sanitation from flooding, which carries the shelter standard, the furthest from reach in Suriname.

register.name: Strengthening Flood Early Warning Systems in Suriname
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · 13 May 2026 · grant financed by the European Union under the Intra-ACP EU Disaster Risk Reduction Programme
register.note: For flood-prone areas including Brokopondo, Sipaliwini, parts of Paramaribo, the Boven-Suriname watershed and coastal zones
register.text: A grant that upgrades weather and river monitoring and forecasting, maps flood risk in 3D and sends timelier warnings through a Common Alerting Protocol, with public education. Earlier warnings protect lives, homes, food security and jobs in the areas most exposed to floods.

register.name: Senior loan to Finabank for small enterprises
register.detail: IDB Invest · approved 7 January 2025 · signed 19 March 2025 · seven-year senior loan · project 15068-01
register.note: For loans to micro, small and medium enterprises, with a special focus on women-led firms
register.text: A seven-year IDB Invest loan of up to $15 million that lets Finabank expand its lending to small and medium-sized enterprises in Suriname. Credit for small firms, women-led ones above all, carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: Bio-SWEET: water, energy and telecommunications for Indigenous villages
register.detail: IDB · approved 2 October 2024 · first $45M loan of a $135M conditional credit line in two tranches · 23.5 years, seven years’ grace · with a $1.5M grant · project SU-L1076
register.note: Expected to benefit 1,200 households, 25 health centres, 30 schools and 50 commercial activities, and 400 women with bioeconomy jobs
register.text: An IDB loan for disaster-resilient solar mini-grids, water collection, treatment and distribution systems and telecommunications in villages of the Amazon interior, with support for the bioeconomy. It carries the water, energy and livelihood standards where the national grid and piped water do not reach.

register.name: Financing Program for Productive and Sustainable Development
register.detail: IDB · approved 16 February 2024 · sovereign-guaranteed loan · credit through the National Development Bank of Suriname (NOB) · project SU-L1069
register.note: Working capital and investment credit for about 500 micro and small businesses; the IDB signing release gives $12 million
register.text: An IDB loan that strengthens the National Development Bank of Suriname so that it can lend to micro, small and medium enterprises for working capital and productive investment, with an emphasis on bio-businesses in agriculture and ecotourism. It carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: GranMorgu development, Block 58
register.detail: TotalEnergies (operator) and APA Corporation, 50% each at the decision · decision 1 October 2024 · production unit of 220,000 barrels of oil a day
register.text: Offshore oil development on Block 58, with a production unit of 220,000 barrels of oil a day; first oil is expected in 2028. Staatsolie, owned by the state, is financing a twenty percent participation in it.
register.note: Staatsolie, the state oil company, is financing a twenty percent participation

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Oil and Gas
items.label: Of GDP from oil and gas rents, 2021
items.text: Oil and gas already earn; the task is to turn the rent into assets that outlast it.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 25.3% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: Surivit
items.text: A social cooperative enterprise that turns fruit and cassava into cassava flour, baby porridge, pancake mixes and flakes for local use and export, with women’s empowerment, especially of Indigenous women, at the heart of its mission; a $300,000 grant from the World Bank-financed SURGE project paid for a processing line, freezing facility and dry storage.

items.name: BOSAQ
items.text: A Belgian water-technology company whose solar-powered, remotely monitored units purify surface water into drinking water; the systems it built gave more than 600 residents of Gunsi, Akwaukonde and Gran Slee in Upper Suriname continuous access to clean, safe water from February 2025.

items.name: Lobi Health Center Foundation
items.text: A non-profit health centre in Paramaribo that promotes sexual and reproductive health, with comprehensive sexuality education run in recent years with UNFPA; its out-of-school training reached about 102 adolescent parents, caregivers and teachers in a year.

items.name: Wi! Uma fu Sranan
items.text: A women’s cooperative that supports Indigenous women in agricultural enterprise, and from which the cassava and fruit processor Surivit was formed.

coverage.gap_text: Of Surinamese lack safely managed sanitation.

guarantees.note: Not food insecure; 35.8% are moderately or severely food insecure

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Safely managed sanitation; 15.8% of city dwellers live in slums

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 95% cook with clean fuels and technology; 99% have electricity

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 42.3% of young people complete lower secondary school

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$8.30 a day; 20.9% live below it
